english.title: Disclose information relating to a persons identity without prior consent of Commissioners
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, contravened article 45(3) of the Plant Health (England) Order 2015 in that you disclosed information received from the Commissioners for His Majesty's Revenue and Customs under article 45(1) of that Order, where the

(A)_[information related to a person whose identity was specified in the disclosure,]_
(B)_[information related to a person whose identity could be deduced from the disclosure,]_

the disclosure being for a purpose other than specified in article 45(1) of the Order and the Commissioners having not given their prior consent to the disclosure
english.legislation: Contrary to articles 45(3), 46(1)(a)(xvii) and 47(2) of the Plant Health (England) Order 2015.

english.notes:
(i) Article 46(1) of the Plant Health (England) Order 2015 provides that proof of reasonable excuse lies with the person.
(ii) Article 46(5) provides that where an offence under the Plant Health (England) Order is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or to have been attributable to any neglect on the part of (a) any director, manager or secretary or other similar officer of the body corporate; or (b) any person who was purporting to act in any such capacity, the person, as well as the body corporate, is guilty of the offence and is liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
(iii) Article 46(6) states for the purposes of Article 46(5), "director" in relation to a body corporate whose affairs are managed by its members, includes a member of the body corporate.
(iv) Article 46(7) provides that Where an offence under this Order is committed by a Scottish partnership and is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or to have been attributable to any neglect on the part of, a partner, the partner, as well as the partnership, is guilty of the offence and is liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
(v) Article 46(8) states that Where the commission by any person of an offence under this Order is due to the act of default of some other person, that other person may be charged with and convicted of the offence by virtue of this paragraph whether or not proceedings for the offence are taken against the first-mentioned person.
(vi) Article 45(3) provides that the defendant may be a crown servant.
(vii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
